base: wsman-tls b959ee8 (pull request 9), on wsman-backend be9965a (pull request 5)
scope: Kerberos authentication and Kerberos message sealing for WS-Management over HTTP (5985) and HTTPS (5986) through the GSS framework of macOS, with NTLM fallback

realm.name: CONTOSO.COM
realm.kdc: Windows Server domain controller, reached as tcp/127.0.0.1:1088 through an SSH tunnel
realm.krb5_conf: [libdefaults] default_realm = CONTOSO.COM, dns_lookup_kdc = false, dns_lookup_realm = false; [realms] CONTOSO.COM kdc = tcp/127.0.0.1:1088; [domain_realm] .contoso.com and contoso.com = CONTOSO.COM; selected with KRB5_CONFIG

listener.host: Windows Server 2025 Datacenter Evaluation 10.0.26100, domain member cm01.contoso.com

winrm_service.Auth/CbtHardeningLevel: Relaxed; Strict for the binding runs; Auth/Kerberos false for the service-refusal runs; both restored and read back

listener.https: 5986 through 127.0.0.1:25988, self-signed certificate CN=cm01.contoso.com, SAN DNS cm01.contoso.com, DNS CM01, IP <server>, trusted with WMIC_WSMAN_CA_FILE

client: Mac mini, Apple M4, macOS 26.6.2, final release build of this branch, /node:cm01.contoso.com, WMIC_WSMAN_CONNECT=127.0.0.1, WMIC_WSMAN_PORT set to the tunnel port, password piped to the prompt

mechanism.client_scheme: Kerberos (raw RFC 4121 token from gss_init_sec_context with the Kerberos mechanism, not SPNEGO)
mechanism.server_scheme: Kerberos (HTTP 200 with a WWW-Authenticate reply token; mutual authentication completed before the first envelope)
mechanism.wrap_token: gss_wrap returned EC 0 and RRC 0; after the 16-byte token header the encrypted part was 44 bytes longer than the plaintext (one Enumerate: plaintext 1324 bytes, token 1384 bytes); the build sent RRC 28, a 60-byte signature and a data part of the plaintext length; the service accepted it and its replies unwrapped through gss_unwrap

runs.then: klist -l; /authority:Kerberos without /user and without a password, same SSH session
runs.result: one row, exit 0; klist -l lists no cache of LabAdmin; the second command exits 186

runs.cache: kinit in the same SSH session
kinit in the same SSH session

runs.kdc_security_log: event 4771, status 0x18, one per run (3 runs)
runs.server_security_log: no 4624 or 4625 with package NTLM for the account

server_events.source: Security log of the host, event 4624, logon type 3, source address <tunnel host>, during the matrix

credential_errors.cferror_code: the GSS major status (851968, GSS_S_FAILURE, in every measured case)
credential_errors.credential_cache: the password logon creates a cache of its own and gss_destroy_cred removes it; klist -l afterward lists no cache of the account; the API cache of the login session is per SSH connection

runs.note: a password with a hyphen also printed Invalid Global Switch.: classic WMIC reads '-' as a switch prefix

ffi_review.headers: GSS.framework of the macOS 26 SDK: gssapi.h, gssapi_apple.h, gssapi_protos.h
ffi_review.struct_packing: gssapi.h applies #pragma pack(push,2) only under defined(__APPLE__) with ppc, ppc64, i386 or x86_64; gss_OID_desc and gss_channel_bindings_struct are declared packed(2) on x86_64 and with the C layout on arm64
ffi_review.symbols: gss_acquire_cred_with_password is exported but not declared in the public headers and is not used

re_measured_after_a_concurrent_session_c.context: a second session ran the same work on the same Mac checkout and lab at the same time; it was stopped and the two disputed facts were measured again alone
re_measured_after_a_concurrent_session_c.channel_binding: a flipped Kerberos binding is refused under Relaxed and Strict (B2); the other session had reported acceptance under Strict with a build started with WMIC_BREAK_BINDING=1; that build returned a row in this measurement with Kerberos and with the KDC not configured, while a flipped binding is refused for Kerberos (B2) and for NTLM (wsman-tls.json), so its switch most likely did not change the binding
re_measured_after_a_concurrent_session_c.kGSSMinorErrorCode: present in the CFError user info as a CFNumber (SInt32) for a wrong password, an unknown client and an unreachable KDC; an earlier dump in this session missed it because its output was cut to four lines
